can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of modal auxiliary verbs ('can', 'will', 'would').
example_raw:
Can you bring some music with you to the dinner. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2008; Bengali; Pass)

I'll be very happy to help you. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Romanian; Pass)

I would like to eat some Spanish food. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2006; Italian; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using basic modals can, will, would

positives: Can you bring some music with you?
I'll be very happy to help you today.
negatives: I am able to bring some music.
She wants to be very happy.

example_raw:
I am 22 years old. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2008; Bengali; Pass)

There are 4 rooms. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Tamil; Pass)

And I like my home because it's not too big and it's a very nice flat. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Tamil; Pass)

It was very nice. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2007; Urdu; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'be' as a main linking verb

positives: It is a very nice apartment.
negatives: I am walking to the park.
The car was stolen last night.

can_do_statement: Can use regular and irregular main verbs in simple verb phrases. ► present simple ► past simple
example_raw:
You know, I love your cooking! (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2006; Slovak; Pass)

I have very good friends. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Polish; Pass)

She comes from India. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2006; Nepali; Pass)

She has long, dark hair and brown eyes. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2006; Polish; Pass)

He gets up at 6 o'clock and goes to work. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2006; Polish; Pass)

I heard from our neighbours about you. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Arabic - Other; Pass)

My grandmother lived in a village and I often went there. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2007; Polish; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using basic present or past main verbs

positives: She lived in a small village.
negatives: He has been waiting for hours.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of modal auxiliary verbs.
example_raw:
And I think we should go somewhere else to have a drink after the film. (Vietnam; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2003; Vietnamese; Pass)

Please wear some of your old and torn clothes because they might get dirty. (India; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Hindi; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using a wider range of modals like should and might

positives: I think we should go somewhere else.

can_do_statement: Can use linking verbs with adjective complements.
example_raw:
It makes me feel comfortable and the room looks bigger with the colour. (Thailand; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Thai; Pass)

My bedroom will be blue because the colour blue always looks fresh and I like it if it's always fresh. (Poland; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Polish; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using linking verbs other than be

positives: The room looks bigger with the new color.
The color blue always looks fresh.
negatives: I look at the sky every night.
We will look into the matter.

example_raw:
It has been a long time since I saw you. (Cyprus; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2003; Greek; Pass)

I have left my suitcase in your house. (India; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; Hindi; Pass)

Have you got a mobile phone? (Italy; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Italian; Pass)

I haven't emailed you in a long time. (India; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Tamil; Pass)

[responding to a question] Yes, I do. I am really excited about the idea. (Mexico; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2002; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

Do you like shopping? (France; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; French; Pass)

Did you buy a new mobile phone? (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Spanish - European; Pass)

I thought that I wouldn't find nice clothes for me, but surprisingly, I did. (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Spanish - European; Pass)

Why didn't you come to my birthday party? (Sri Lanka; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; Singhalese; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using have and do as auxiliaries

positives: I have left my suitcase in your house.

can_do_statement: Can use semi-modal auxiliary verbs, 'dare' and 'need'.
example_raw:
You needn't worry about where we can stay. (China; B2 VANTAGE; 1998; Chinese; Pass)

I think that they are rather jealous because they daren't give up their car. (France; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; French; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using dare and need as modals

positives: You needn't worry about the cost.
She daren't speak to him again.
negatives: You don't need to worry about the cost.

guideword: FORM: SEMI-MODAL AUXILIARY VERBS, 'USED TO', 'OUGHT TO'
can_do_statement: Can use semi-modal auxiliary verbs, 'used to' and 'ought to'.
example_raw:
But we used to play together every single day! (Japan; B1 THRESHOLD; 1999; Japanese; Pass)

I think you ought to join a gym and you should go for a walk at least three times a week. (Libya; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Arabic - Meghreb; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using used to and ought to

positives: We used to play together every day.
You ought to join a gym soon.
negatives: I am used to playing with them.
The tool was used to fix the car.

can_do_statement: Can use semi-modal auxiliary verb 'have (got) to'.
example_raw:
You've got to bring paintbrushes, paper and paint, that's all. (Vietnam; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; French; Pass)

You don't have to bring anything except your clothes. (Greece; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Greek; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using have got to or have to

positives: You don't have to bring anything.
negatives: I have a lot of things to do.
She has got a new car to drive.
